_comments.source: Hand-curated 2026-04-05. Primary headache disorder, managed on a spectrum from OTC meds to CGRP antagonists to botulinum toxin injections (chronic migraine) to occipital nerve blocks.
_comments.hcpcs_rationale: 64615 chemodenervation of head/neck muscles is the chronic-migraine Botox CPT (the PREEMPT protocol). J0585 is the onabotulinumtoxinA drug code billed alongside. 64405 occipital nerve block and 64400 face nerve (trigeminal branch) injections are in-office procedures done for migraine. 99213/99214/99215 E&M drive the majority of neurology visit volume for this condition (high-touch chronic care). Note: this is one of the few neurology-chronic conditions with a meaningful procedural signal, distinguishing it from HTN/T2DM.
_comments.taxonomy_rationale: Neurology (including Vascular Neurology and Pain Medicine sub-certs) is the primary specialty. PM&R Pain Medicine, Anesthesiology Pain Medicine, and standalone Pain Medicine taxonomies also do headache procedures. Family Medicine and Internal Medicine manage non-refractory cases.
_comments.pubmed_rationale: Core condition and treatment names, including newer drug classes (CGRP), procedural treatments (Botox, nerve block), and prophylaxis vs acute.
